title: C# Questions & Answers - Try & Catch in Detail
sourceFile: Try & Catch - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on detail of try & catch in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What is the primary use of 'try' and 'catch' blocks in C#?

options.text: It is used to manually handle runtime exceptions
It helps in identifying and handling runtime errors
It prevents the program from terminating abruptly when an error occurs

questions.explanation: The try-catch mechanism allows programmers to catch runtime errors (exceptions) and provide alternative logic, ensuring the application can recover or exit gracefully instead of crashing.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Since 9/5 equals 1 in integer arithmetic, no DivideByZeroException occurs. The try block prints 'Hello', the catch block is skipped, and the finally block always executes, printing 'sharp'.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 'try' block is INCORRECT?

options.text: A try block does not necessarily need to be followed by a catch block
A try block can be followed by a finally block instead of a catch block
A try block can be followed by both catch and finally blocks
A try block can exist without any following catch or finally block

questions.explanation: In C#, a 'try' block must be followed by at least one 'catch' block or one 'finally' block. It cannot stand alone; otherwise, a compile-time error occurs.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: No exception is thrown during the calculation. The program executes the code in the try block sequentially, printing 'Hi', and skips the catch block.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a block of code to be monitored for exceptions?
questions.explanation: The 'try' keyword signals the start of a guarded section of code where exceptions might occur and need to be handled.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a block that handles a specific exception generated by the try block?
questions.explanation: The 'catch' block contains the error-handling code. It only executes if an exception matching the specified type occurs in the preceding try block.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to manually signal the occurrence of an exception during program execution?
questions.explanation: In C#, the 'throw' keyword is used to explicitly raise an exception, either to re-throw a caught error or to trigger a new custom exception.
